focusSummary: Switching between casual plain forms and polite register, softening speech with 〜けど and explaining reasons with 〜から, and warm neighborhood banter with hosts or shopkeepers.

lessonSteps.heading: Plain Form vs. Polite Register in Everyday Banter
lessonSteps.explanation: Close friends and welcoming guesthouse hosts often speak in plain form (いく instead of いきます, いい天気だね instead of いい天気ですね). Even when someone speaks casually to you, replying in warm です/ます with ね ('isn't it?') sounds friendly without overstepping.
lessonSteps.scenarioPrompt: Your guesthouse host smiles over morning coffee and says 「今日、いい天気だね！どこ行くの？」 ('Nice weather today, huh! Where are you heading?').
lessonSteps.nativeText: ほんとうにいい天気ですね。ちょっと近所を散歩します。
lessonSteps.rubyHtml: ほんとうにいい<ruby>天気<rt>てんき</rt></ruby>ですね。ちょっと<ruby>近所<rt>きんじょ</rt></ruby>を<ruby>散歩<rt>さんぽ</rt></ruby>します。
lessonSteps.romanization: Hontō ni ii tenki desu ne. Chotto kinjo o sanpo shimasu.
lessonSteps.translation: It really is nice weather, isn't it? I'm going to stroll around the neighborhood for a bit.
lessonSteps.literalBreakdown: ほんとうに (really) + いい天気 (good weather) + ですね (is, right?) / ちょっと (a little) + 近所を (neighborhood) + 散歩します (stroll)
lessonSteps.usageTip: ちょっと literally means 'a little', but in conversation it makes actions sound relaxed and unpretentious.

lessonSteps.heading: Giving Natural Reasons with 〜から
lessonSteps.explanation: Attach から ('because / since') right after a clause to explain why you are doing something. In friendly polite conversation, plain-form + から before a polite main verb feels natural and unforced.
lessonSteps.scenarioPrompt: A local bakery owner offers you a plastic bag, and you explain why you don't need one.
lessonSteps.nativeText: エコバッグがあるから、大丈夫です！
lessonSteps.romanization: Ekobaggu ga aru kara, daijōbu desu!
lessonSteps.translation: Since I have a reusable tote bag, I'm all set!
lessonSteps.literalBreakdown: エコバッグ (eco-bag) + がある (exists/have, plain form) + から (because/so) + 大丈夫です (I'm fine)
lessonSteps.usageTip: Putting plain form (ある) rather than あります inside the 〜から clause keeps the sentence from sounding stiffly repetitive.

lessonSteps.heading: Trailing Off & Opening Requests Softly with 〜けど
lessonSteps.explanation: けど ('though / but') isn't just for contrast—Japanese speakers constantly use 〜んですけど as a gentle conversational opener to introduce context before asking a question or favor.
lessonSteps.scenarioPrompt: You step into a small neighborhood coffee roaster and want to ask for a recommendation.
lessonSteps.nativeText: コーヒーを買いたいんですけど、どれが人気ですか。
lessonSteps.rubyHtml: コーヒーを<ruby>買<rt>か</rt></ruby>いたいんですけど、どれが<ruby>人気<rt>にんき</rt></ruby>ですか。
lessonSteps.romanization: Kōhī o kaitai n desu kedo, dore ga ninki desu ka.
lessonSteps.translation: I'd like to buy some coffee—which one is popular?
lessonSteps.literalBreakdown: コーヒーを買いたい (want to buy coffee) + んですけど (it's that..., softening lead-in) + どれが人気ですか (which is popular?)
lessonSteps.usageTip: 〜んですけど signals 'here is my situation—could you help me out?' and invites the listener into the conversation.

lessonSteps.heading: Warm Parting Phrases with Shopkeepers & Hosts
lessonSteps.explanation: When leaving a guesthouse in the morning, say いってきます ('I'm heading out and coming back'), and the host replies いってらっしゃい ('Have a safe outing'). With a friendly neighborhood shopkeeper you plan to visit again, また来ます ('I'll come again!') lights up faces.
lessonSteps.scenarioPrompt: You finish chatting with the owner of a corner bakery near your stay.
lessonSteps.nativeText: おいしそうですね！ありがとうございます、また来ます。
lessonSteps.rubyHtml: おいしそうですね！ありがとうございます、また<ruby>来<rt>き</rt></ruby>ます。
lessonSteps.romanization: Oishisō desu ne! Arigatō gozaimasu, mata kimasu.
lessonSteps.translation: That looks delicious! Thank you very much—I'll come by again.
lessonSteps.literalBreakdown: おいしそう (looks delicious) + ですね (doesn't it!) + ありがとうございます + また (again) + 来ます (will come)
lessonSteps.usageTip: Verb/i-adjective stem + そう (おいしそう = looks tasty, よさそう = looks good) is effortless small-talk gold in shops.

drills.prompt: You want to explain to the clerk that you don't need a bag BECAUSE you brought your backpack (リュックがある). Choose the natural sentence:
drills.cue: Connect the reason clause with から
options: リュックがあるを、袋は大丈夫です。
リュックがあるから、袋は大丈夫です。
リュックがあるどこ、袋は大丈夫です。
リュックがあるへ、袋は大丈夫です。
drills.correctAnswer: リュックがあるから、袋は大丈夫です。
drills.explanation: Clause + から expresses cause/reason ('Since I have my backpack, I'm good without a bag').

drills.prompt: You walk into a neighborhood tea shop and want to preface your question softly: 'I'm looking for a gift, so...' Complete the opener:
drills.baseSentence: おみやげを探しているんです＿＿＿、どれがいいですか。
drills.explanation: 〜んですけど gently sets the scene for a request without sounding abrupt or demanding.

drills.prompt: Your guesthouse host calls out 「いってらっしゃい！」 as you step out the front door in the morning. What had you naturally just said—or can say back?
drills.cue: Standard phrase when heading out from your home base
drills.explanation: いってきます ('I'll go and come back') pairs with the host's いってらっしゃい ('Go and come back safely').

srsCards.contextTranslation: I shopped at the neighborhood bakery and chatted for a bit.

gradedStories.title: 近所のパン屋さんと朝の会話
gradedStories.titleTranslation: Morning Small Talk at the Neighborhood Bakery
gradedStories.setting: A sunny morning strolling from a Kyoto machiya guesthouse to a corner bakery.

paragraphs.nativeText: ゲストハウスを出るとき、オーナーの田中さんに「いってきます！」と言いました。田中さんは「今日はいい天気だから、散歩にぴったりだね。いってらっしゃい！」と笑いました。
paragraphs.rubyHtml: ゲストハウスを<ruby>出<rt>で</rt></ruby>るとき、オーナーの<ruby>田中<rt>たなか</rt></ruby>さんに「いってきます！」と<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>いました。<ruby>田中<rt>たなか</rt></ruby>さんは「<ruby>今日<rt>きょう</rt></ruby>はいい<ruby>天気<rt>てんき</rt></ruby>だから、<ruby>散歩<rt>さんぽ</rt></ruby>にぴったりだね。いってらっしゃい！」と<ruby>笑<rt>わら</rt></ruby>いました。
paragraphs.translation: When heading out of the guesthouse, I called out 'I'm heading out!' to the owner, Tanaka-san. Tanaka-san smiled and said, 'Since the weather's great today, it's perfect for a walk. Have a great time!'

paragraphs.nativeText: 近所の小さなパン屋さんに入って、「朝ごはんを買いたいんですけど、どれが人気ですか」と聞きました。お店の人は「焼きたてのカレーパンが一番人気ですよ」と話してくれました。
paragraphs.rubyHtml: <ruby>近所<rt>きんじょ</rt></ruby>の<ruby>小<rt>ちい</rt></ruby>さなパン<ruby>屋<rt>や</rt></ruby>さんに<ruby>入<rt>はい</rt></ruby>って、「<ruby>朝<rt>あさ</rt></ruby>ごはんを<ruby>買<rt>か</rt></ruby>いたいんですけど、どれが<ruby>人気<rt>にんき</rt></ruby>ですか」と<ruby>聞<rt>き</rt></ruby>きました。お<ruby>店<rt>みせ</rt></ruby>の<ruby>人<rt>ひと</rt></ruby>は「<ruby>焼<rt>や</rt></ruby>きたてのカレーパンが<ruby>一番<rt>いちばん</rt></ruby><ruby>人気<rt>にんき</rt></ruby>ですよ」と<ruby>話<rt>はな</rt></ruby>してくれました。
paragraphs.translation: Stepping into a tiny neighborhood bakery, I asked, 'I'd like to buy breakfast—which one is popular?' The baker told me, 'Our freshly baked curry bread is the number-one favorite!'

paragraphs.nativeText: 「じゃあ、それをお願いします。かばんがあるから、袋は大丈夫です」と言って買いました。「ありがとうございます、また来ます！」と言うと、お店の人もにっこりしました。
paragraphs.rubyHtml: 「じゃあ、それをお<ruby>願<rt>ねが</rt></ruby>いします。かばんがあるから、<ruby>袋<rt>ふくろ</rt></ruby>は<ruby>大丈夫<rt>だいじょうぶ</rt></ruby>です」と<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>って<ruby>買<rt>か</rt></ruby>いました。「ありがとうございます、また<ruby>来<rt>き</rt></ruby>ます！」と<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>うと、お<ruby>店<rt>みせ</rt></ruby>の<ruby>人<rt>ひと</rt></ruby>もにっこりしました。
paragraphs.translation: 'Well then, I'll take that please. Since I have my bag, I'm fine without a shopping bag,' I said and bought it. When I added 'Thank you, I'll come again!', the shopkeeper beamed.

segments.reading: ありがとうございます

questions.question: Why did Tanaka-san say it was an ideal day for a walk?
options: Because the weather was nice today
Because the bakery was closing early
questions.explanation: Tanaka-san said 「今日はいい天気だから、散歩にぴったりだね」 ('Since the weather is nice today, it's perfect for a walk').

questions.question: What did the baker recommend as their most popular item?
options: Freshly baked curry bread (焼きたてのカレーパン)
questions.explanation: The baker replied 「焼きたてのカレーパンが一番人気ですよ」.

questions.question: Why did the narrator decline a shopping bag?
options: They ate the bread inside the bakery
They already had their own bag/satchel (かばんがあるから)
questions.explanation: They explained 「かばんがあるから、袋は大丈夫です」 ('Since I have my bag, I'm fine without a bag').
